notes: Overall a solid implementation with good structure, but has meaningful architectural violations. ARCHITECTURAL ISSUES: (1) CommentService directly depends on ITaskService and IUserService via constructor injection and calls their methods directly (comment-service.ts lines: taskService.getById, userService.getById) — this is a direct service-to-service call violating Rule 1; the comment payload should be assembled by the caller or the event should carry sufficient data. (2) NotificationService directly calls taskService.getById in handleCommentAdded — another direct service-to-service call violating Rule 1; the CommentAddedPayload already carries taskTitle but not assigneeId, requiring this cross-service lookup. The fix would be to include assigneeId in CommentAddedPayload. CONSTRAINT VIOLATIONS: Rule 1 violated twice as described. Rule 2 is satisfied. Rule 3 (HTTP only in router) is satisfied. Rule 4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly implemented with allowedTransitions map. Rule 5 (no npm deps) is satisfied. Rule 6 (each service in own file) is satisfied. COMPLETENESS: All CRUD operations are present for all entities. All three events (task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added) are published and subscribed. Demo script covers all major flows. Minor gap: GET /tasks without projectId filter returns nothing useful; no validation on required fields (e.g., missing name/email on user creation). DELETE /projects/:id/members uses request body which is non-standard for DELETE. No email uniqueness validation. CODE QUALITY: Good use of TypeScript interfaces in types.ts, clean separation of concerns, consistent error throwing with descriptive messages. The router is verbose but functional. handleSuccess returning void for undefined creates a subtle control-flow issue (no early return after calling handleError). The router's if-else chain is long but manageable. IEventBus uses unknown type correctly. Missing input validation throughout services.
